questions.note: Order reads right for the scope: the hallux is longest and toe 2 several mm shorter, curled with its PIP raised in profile (toes 3–5 out of scope). Shaping is weak: toe 2 is an even tube in plan with no PIP swelling or waist; both knuckles carry the same stamped groove set; toe 2 has a plantar cuff ledge and the hallux a hard V-notch at its IP crease and a flat, shallow section.

Hallux and toe 2 nails only. Free-edge thickness and a fold rim are there and the corners no longer tear, but both read as press-ons: rounded-rectangle tiles in an even gutter with a gasket rim, nearly flat across, an opaque cream French-tip edge that waves instead of being cut straight, no lunula, a milky plate with no pink bed, and brushed-metal streaks.

Only the forefoot is in frame (no V1/V2; the saphenous is out of view). There the extensor ridges are faint and fade out before the MTPs: no EHL relief onto the hallux, no slip to toe 2, no dorsal veins. The only relief over the first MTP is a raised, glossy scar-like line. Beside the anchor feet the dorsum reads as a smooth mannequin surface.

Material is declared a first pass; scored as seen. Shadow sides stay dark, no glow. But the micro-relief is wrong in kind: a crazed-glaze net of dark-outlined polygons about 0.4–0.8 mm (twice the toes' 0.25–0.4) everywhere, plantar ridges as one-angle diagonal stripes with no whorls on the pads, no follicle pits, and a broad oily gloss on the dorsum.

defects.what: The hallux nail is a template rounded-rectangle tile sunk in an even gutter and ringed by a raised gasket rim, its top nearly flat across: an inset panel or press-on, not a plate growing out from under the folds.
defects.fix: Dome the plate to its 11 mm transverse radius so its sides roll down under lateral folds that overlap them, and let the proximal fold lie on the plate with a thin cuticle, with no gutter or rim around it.

defects.what: The hallux free edge is an opaque, even, milky-cream band with a rolled bead whose line waves in an S, dipping medially and rising to an upturned lateral corner: a French-manicure tip, not a toenail trimmed straight across.
defects.fix: Trimmed straight across with slightly rounded corners: a thin, slightly irregular off-white edge, translucent (transmission about 0.7), 1.5 mm beyond the hyponychium, with a faint grime line under it.

defects.what: The hallux plate is one milky grey-pink from root to free edge: no lunula at the proximal end and no pink bed showing through a clear plate, so it reads as frosted acrylic rather than nail.
defects.fix: A clear plate over a pink bed (#d49a88), a pale 3.5 mm lunula crescent at the proximal fold, and the paler free edge only beyond the hyponychium.

defects.what: Toe 2's nail, like the hallux's, is combed with bold white longitudinal streaks through every highlight, like brushed metal.
defects.fix: Real ridging is about 0.01 mm deep at 0.25 mm pitch: a faint ripple seen only where a highlight grazes the plate.

defects.what: Toe 2 is an even tube about 14.5 mm wide from the PIP to the pulp: no PIP condyle swelling, no waist over the middle phalanx and no pulp flare in plan, a sausage toe beside the anchor feet's knuckled second toes.
defects.fix: Broadest at the PIP knuckle, waisted over the short middle phalanx, the pulp flaring again under the nail.

defects.what: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: three or four identical, evenly spaced, parallel grooves of equal depth, like bellows, proud enough to bump the profile in the medial view.
defects.fix: A loose cluster of fine creases of unequal length, spacing and depth, some broken or branching, fading out toward the sides, about 0.2 mm deep.

defects.what: Toe 2's dorsal DIP crease is a single long, even groove with a bright lip right across the toe: a knife cut rather than a skin crease.
defects.fix: Two or three short, soft, uneven creases over the DIP that fade out at the sides.

defects.what: Under toe 2 a straight, sharp-edged ledge crosses the whole toe at the PIP crease, the distal part stepping out like a sleeve cuff, smooth above and ridged below.
defects.fix: A soft flexion crease with the skin and its ridges running on across it and the pad swelling smoothly beyond.

defects.what: In profile the hallux's plantar outline is pinched into a sharp V-notch with a hard lip at its IP crease, the pulp stepping down below the proximal phalanx as if a second tube were plugged on.
defects.fix: A shallow, soft dimple in a continuous curve from the proximal pad to the pulp.

defects.what: A thin, raised, glossy line arcs about 15 mm across the first MTP dorsum and bumps the profile in the medial view: it reads as a healed incision scar.
defects.fix: Smooth skin over the joint, or a few short, soft transverse wrinkles that fade out.

defects.what: From below the hallux flows straight out of the ball with no base sulcus; its only crease is at the IP, so nothing marks where the toe pad meets the ball.
defects.fix: A deep, curved digito-plantar fold where the hallux pad meets the ball, at about the level of the 1–2 web.

defects.what: The hallux is broad but shallow: about 30 mm across in the front and plantar views yet only about 20–21 mm deep at the IP and 18 at the nail root in profile, so it reads flattened and spatulate rather than round.
defects.fix: Jeff's direction thickens the toe by half the width's share, to about 25 mm deep at the IP, so the pad stays round.

defects.what: The 1–2 web reads as a flat shelf between the toes with a straight, flat-bottomed margin, rather than a soft U-shaped saddle sunk between their bases.
defects.fix: A narrow, concave U-shaped commissure set back between the toes' bases, its margin curving up into both toes' sides.

defects.what: Below the hallux nail's medial distal corner a short red vertical slit runs down onto the pulp, a pinch that also shows as a crease in clay.
defects.fix: The lateral nail groove ends at the free edge's corner; the hyponychium and pulp skin run on unbroken below it.

defects.what: The free edge's lateral corner is a squared, upturned tab resting on the skin, with a thin pale seam running down from it.
defects.fix: A slightly rounded corner lying in the lateral groove, the free edge standing just clear of the skin with a thin shadow under it.

defects.what: No hair: no tuft on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2; the bald, clean toes read young and mannequin-like beside the hairier anchor feet.
defects.fix: 8–12 dark brown hairs 5–8 mm long lying flat distally on the hallux's proximal phalanx, and 2–4 shorter ones on toe 2's.

defects.what: Tendons and veins are nearly absent: faint extensor ridges on the forefoot fade out well before the MTPs, no EHL runs onto the hallux, no slip to toe 2, and no dorsal veins in frame.
defects.fix: The EHL as 0.5–1.5 mm relief running to the hallux's distal phalanx, the EDL slip to toe 2, and low dorsal digital veins that catch the light.

ranked: [D1] The hallux nail, the focus of most views, is a press-on: a template rounded-rectangle tile set in an even gutter with a raised gasket rim and nearly flat across. A real big-toe nail is a domed plate growing out from under the folds, its sides rolling down beneath them.

[D2] Its free edge is a French-manicure tip: an opaque, even cream band with a rolled bead that waves in an S to an upturned lateral corner. A trimmed toenail is cut straight across, thin, translucent off-white and a little irregular.

[D5] Toe 2 is a sausage: an even tube from PIP to pulp with no knuckle swelling, no waist over the middle phalanx and no pulp flare in plan, where the anchor feet's second toes are knuckled and waisted.
[D3] The plates are one milky grey-pink from root to tip: no lunula on the hallux and no pink bed under a clear plate, so they read as frosted acrylic, not nail.

[D6] The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp, three or four identical, evenly spaced parallel grooves like bellows, proud enough to bump the profile; real knuckle skin has a loose, uneven cluster of fine creases.

The skin's micro-relief, declared a first pass, still colours every closeup in scope: a crazed-glaze net of dark-outlined polygons about 0.4–0.8 mm, twice the toes' 0.25–0.4 mm, equally deep everywhere, so the toes read as porcelain or dried mud, not skin.
[D4] Every highlight on both nails is combed into bold white longitudinal streaks, like brushed metal; real ridging is a faint ripple seen only where a highlight grazes the plate.

[D8] Under toe 2 the PIP crease is a straight, sharp ledge across the whole toe, the distal part stepping out like a sleeve cuff, smooth above and ridged below: the same cuff the untouched toes 3 and 4 still carry.

[D9] In profile the hallux's plantar outline is pinched into a hard V-notch at its IP crease, the pulp stepping down as if a second tube were plugged on; a real toe shows a soft dimple in a continuous curve.
[D10] A thin, raised, glossy line arcs about 15 mm across the first MTP dorsum and bumps the medial profile: a podiatrist would read a healed incision, not a crease.

[D12] The hallux is broad but shallow, about 30 mm across yet only about 20–21 mm deep at the IP, so in profile it reads flattened and spatulate; Jeff's direction thickens it to about 25 mm so the pad stays round.
[D11] From below the hallux flows straight out of the ball with no base sulcus, its only crease at the IP; a real sole folds deeply where the toe pad meets the ball, at about the level of the web.
[D13] The 1–2 web reads as a flat shelf with a straight, flat-bottomed margin between the toes rather than a soft U-shaped saddle sunk between their bases.
[D7] Toe 2's dorsal DIP crease is a single long, even groove with a bright lip, a knife cut; a real DIP shows two or three short, soft, uneven creases.

The plantar friction ridges, also first-pass material, are straight diagonal stripes at one angle over the ball and both pads, running through the creases like corduroy; real pads carry whorls and loops and the ridges bend along the creases.

[D17] The forefoot dorsum in frame is a smooth mannequin surface: faint extensor ridges fade out before the MTPs, no EHL runs onto the hallux, no slip to toe 2 and no dorsal veins, where the anchor feet show both as low relief.
[D16] No hair: no tuft on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2. Bald toes read young; several anchor feet carry dark hairs there.

The toes read too young and clean for a boot-wearing 40-year-old: one even peach tone with no redness at knuckles or tips, no darker creases, no pinch callus on the hallux's medial IP and no grime line under the free edges.
Toe 2's nail repeats the hallux's faults at a smaller scale: a rounded-rectangle tile in an even gutter, a cream French-tip edge and streaked highlights.
A broad, oily gloss over the forefoot dorsum and the toes (first-pass material) adds to the waxy, mannequin read at native size.
[D14] Below the hallux nail's medial distal corner a short red vertical slit runs down onto the pulp, a pinch that also shows as a crease in clay.
[D15] The free edge's lateral corner is a squared, upturned tab resting on the skin with a thin pale seam running down from it, instead of a rounded corner lying in the lateral groove.
